title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
corePattern: Two Pointers with Dummy Head Node
interviewTips: Using a dummy node simplifies pointer logic by eliminating edge cases for the head pointer.
Once one list is exhausted, directly splice the remainder of the other list in O(1).

approaches.name: Approach 1: Iterative with Dummy Node (Optimal)
approaches.intuition: Create a dummy head node. Compare the current nodes of list1 and list2, attach the smaller node to `curr->next`, and advance that list. When one list ends, splice the remaining nodes.
approaches.theory: Because both lists are already sorted, the smallest remaining element is always at either `list1` or `list2`. We merge them in a manner identical to the merge step of Merge Sort.

timeComplexity.explanation: Every iteration advances one of the two list pointers; visits at most N + M nodes.

spaceComplexity.explanation: No new heap nodes created; only rearranges existing pointers.

steps: tail attaches 1 (l1), then 1 (l2), then 2 (l1), then 3 (l2), then 4 (l1), then 4 (l2)

edgeCases: One list is null: returns the other list immediately.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Recursive Divide & Conquer
approaches.intuition: If list1->val < list2->val, list1 becomes head, and list1->next = mergeTwoLists(list1->next, list2).
approaches.theory: Subproblem induction: The head of the merged list is the smaller head, followed by the result of recursively merging the remainder.

timeComplexity.explanation: Recurses once per node until one list terminates.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion call stack frames equal to length of combined lists.

edgeCases: Stack overflow for extremely deep linked lists (N > 10,000).
